subject: Citrine Health - surge impact: throughput, errors, and exec lifeline
messages:
From: Aisha Varma <aisha.varma@citrine.health>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-04T08:12:00Z
Subject: High error-rate + stalled checkout traffic (Citrine)

Hi Grace,

We started seeing a degradation at ~08:05 UTC — elevated 5xx rate on the checkout flow, and an increase in p99 latency from ~220ms to ~2.1s. Throughput looks erratic: bursts followed by timeouts. This is impacting live customers, about ~14% of checkouts failing with retries.

Attached is a short trace (sample-traces-0504.zip) and a screenshot of our monitoring. Can your team engage the on-call and execs? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you can route traffic to a lower-latency fallback.

Thanks,
Aisha Varma
Ops Lead, Citrine Health
ops@citrine.health

Attachments: sample-traces-0504.zip, monitoring-screenshot-08-10.png

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Varma <aisha.varma@citrine.health>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-04T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: High error-rate + stalled checkout traffic (Citrine)

Hi Aisha — thank you for the heads up and the traces. We're standing up a short executive war-room now and will provide a customer-facing update within the next hour. Internal plan in progress: 1) immediate mitigation (routing + autoscale), 2) enable a fallback model variant with lower memory footprint, 3) turn on aggressive prefix caching for the checkout path, 4) capture full KV/trace snapshots.

Could you confirm: are all failing requests going through the same region (us-east-1) and are there any recent config changes on your side? Also please share any recent traffic spikes or promotions.

I'll follow up with timeline + bridge details in 5–10 minutes.

— Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-04T08:25:00Z
Subject: Re: High error-rate + stalled checkout traffic (Citrine)

Grace / team — quick technical note from SRE: we've observed a sudden shift in sequence length distribution for the affected route (median length unchanged, but variance spiked). That is causing suboptimal kernel selection on a subset of hosts and amplified KV-cache misses. Immediate actions we've pushed:

- Increase autoscale policy threshold and spin additional Dedicated instances in the us-east-1 pool (30% extra capacity).
- Apply a hotfix to force the more conservative kernel path for this model family (falls back to the production-friendly kernel).
- Route ~20% of traffic to a quantized 8-bit model variant we validated for compatibility (lower throughput but lower p99).
- Enable aggressive prefix caching and extend cache TTL on checkout prefix keys.

I also triggered a temporary routing policy to keep warm instances for high-concurrency bursts. We'll monitor for 15 mins and provide telemetry dumps.

--Sean
Director of SRE, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Pager: PD-99821

From: Aisha Varma <aisha.varma@citrine.health>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@citrine.health
Date: 2028-05-04T08:34:00Z
Subject: Re: High error-rate + stalled checkout traffic (Citrine)

Grace / Sean — confirmation: this is all us-east-1, no config changes on our side and no promo running. We have around 700 concurrent checkout sessions right now; failures are concentrated on 3rd-party payment calls that time out downstream when Redwood times out. Business impact: estimated $48k ARR revenue at risk during this window.

We appreciate the quick action. Please let us know immediately if you will put a short retry/backoff or circuit-breaker in place toward the payment integration so we don't cascade failures.

—Aisha
Ops Lead, Citrine Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-04T08:40:00Z
Subject: Exec summary & next steps (Citrine impact)

Team — quick executive summary to prep for the bridge and customer comms:

1) Current state: elevated 5xx and p99 latency on Citrine checkout route, concentrated in us-east-1; root cause likely interplay of sequence-length variance and cache churn on a subset of Dedicated hosts.
2) Immediate mitigations (in flight): autoscale spike (+30%), fallback to quantized variant for 20% traffic, hotfix for kernel selection, and aggressive prefix caching.
3) Short-term customer commit: we will: a) prevent further regression by routing and circuit-breaker adjustments, b) restore p99 toward baseline within 30–45 minutes, c) follow with a postmortem within 48 hours with action items.
4) Ask: Marissa, own customer-facing status updates. Sean, validate the hotfix rollout and confirm telemetry for the next 15/30/60 minute marks. Grace, coordinate exec bridge and HubSpot note.

I'll be on the bridge. If anything changes materially (e.g., regression after reroute), escalate to the CTO immediately.

—Laura Bennett
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Varma <aisha.varma@citrine.health>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-04T09:32:00Z
Subject: Citrine update — mitigations applied and next steps (09:32 UTC)

Hi Aisha — quick customer update to confirm what we've done and what's next. Internal team is copied.

What we implemented (complete):
- Autoscale increase in us-east-1 (additional Dedicated capacity engaged).
- Temporary routing policy applied; ~20% of traffic spilled to a validated 8-bit quantized model variant.
- Kernel-path hotfix deployed to the impacted host subset.
- Aggressive prefix caching enabled on checkout keys; cache TTL extended.
- Circuit-breaker applied toward the downstream payment step to reduce retries and prevent cascade.

Immediate impact observed: p99 latency has dropped from ~2.1s to ~420ms in the last 10 minutes; 5xx rate is trending down but not yet baseline. We continue to monitor; Sean's team is watching telemetry and will post 15/30/60 minute snapshots to the bridge.

Next steps and timeline:
- 09:45 UTC: snapshot + short runbook dump posted (runbook-citrine-fallback.pdf).
- 10:30 UTC: if stable, begin gradual rollback of quantized spill and autoscale to baseline over 60 minutes.
- 48 hours: full postmortem and remediation plan (root cause, capacity tuning, and improved rollout policy).

Attachments: runbook-citrine-fallback.pdf, dashboard-snapshot-08-12.png
Bridge link: https://pagerduty.com/incident/PD-99821
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/contact/4821

Thank you for the quick signal and the traces — this helped isolate the distribution shift quickly. We'll deliver the 09:45 snapshot and customer-facing summary.

Regards,
